scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A2 test draft, independently authored with four options per question. Teacher approval pending.

tabs.title: Making a Change
tabs.description: Understand why his plan is useful.

tabs.title: Try It Yourself
tabs.description: Apply the ideas to a new situation.

questions.q: Why is Daniel's usual Wednesday evening not good for him?
choices: He has to travel to another town.
He helps his sister with homework.
He studies too late and feels tired.
He forgets to bring his textbook.
questions.explanation: Paragraph one describes late-night study and tiredness the following day.

questions.q: How is Daniel's plan on Monday different from his old plan?
choices: He studies in a short session and rests.
He waits until Thursday to start.
He studies for three hours without a break.
He asks his sister to take the test.
questions.explanation: Monday contains a twenty-minute session followed by a break.

questions.q: What does Daniel do when he cannot explain an idea?
choices: He decides it is not important.
He asks for a better mark.
He stops studying for the week.
He looks at his notes again.
questions.explanation: In paragraph two he checks the notes when his explanation is not clear.

questions.q: Why does Daniel answer some questions without looking at his notes?
choices: To finish his homework in class.
To check what he knows by himself.
To show his sister the answers.
To avoid using the textbook again.
questions.explanation: Testing himself without notes helps him discover what he remembers.

questions.q: What is Daniel pleased about, apart from his mark?
choices: He misses part of the test.
He never makes mistakes now.
He has slept well and feels calmer.
He has changed his science teacher.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says he is pleased to have slept well and enjoyed Wednesday.

questions.q: Why will Daniel make changes to the plan if needed?
choices: A useful study plan can be improved.
A good study plan must be perfect.
History does not need any practice.
His old plan always worked well.
questions.explanation: The final sentence explains that he will adapt the plan to another subject.

questions.q: Your friend cannot explain a maths idea. What could help?
choices: Study for hours without stopping.
Turn on phone notifications.
Wait for the next test result.
Look at the notes and try an example.
questions.explanation: Daniel checks notes and uses a textbook example when an idea is difficult.

questions.q: Someone says, 'Two mistakes mean the new plan failed.' What would Daniel say?
choices: A plan works only if the mark is perfect.
Mistakes can show what to practise next.
Studying without sleep is always better.
There is no point in changing habits.
questions.explanation: Daniel makes two mistakes but feels calmer and identifies what to practise.

questions.q: How can a student check learning before a quiz?
choices: Answer some questions without the notes.
Copy every answer from the textbook.
Study only the easiest questions.
Leave all the work until late at night.
questions.explanation: Daniel uses practice questions without looking at the answers.

questions.q: What does Daniel really want from his new routine?
choices: To stop learning science.
To spend three hours on every subject.
To prepare well without feeling so tired.
To have someone else check every answer.
questions.explanation: Paragraph one says he wants a calmer day, not only a better mark.
